business_summary: Advanced Micro Devices is a semiconductor company. Revenue grew 13.64% a year over three years and 28.82% over five. FY25 operating margin was 12.17%, 4.95 percentage points above three years earlier. Borrowings are small at 0.05 times equity. Net profit is positive, with no loss-making quarter in the last four.
why_own: The case rests on sustained revenue growth, margins that have widened over three years, and strong cash conversion (1.78 times profit) on a nearly debt-free balance sheet. The evidence is numbers only, with no supplied documents, so there are no qualitative drivers. Returns on capital are modest (ROCE 6.49%) against a trailing P/E of 135.68 times, so the thesis depends on growth continuing.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate (3-year CAGR currently 13.64%).
Operating margin holds the gains of the last three years (12.17% in FY25, up 4.95 percentage points).
Reported profit is backed by cash: operating cash flow stays well above net profit (1.78 times currently). (warn line tightened by code from 1 to 1.25.)
Returns on capital improve from the current low level (ROCE 6.49%) as profit grows.
Return on equity should stay above 10%. (added by code: currently 7.19.)
Trailing P/E should stay below 60x, or the price needs years of flawless growth. (added by code: currently 135.68.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 6%, which would erase most of the three-year margin gain.
Operating cash flow falls below half of net profit.

risks.statement: Valuation is demanding: trailing P/E is 135.68 times and price/book is 13.86 times, so little room for growth or margin disappointment. The comparison with the stock's own 5-year P/E history is not available.
Returns on capital are low (ROCE 6.49%, ROE 7.19%) relative to the price paid for the equity. Why they are low has not been tested with this evidence.

Growth is slowing from the longer-term pace (3-year revenue CAGR 13.64% against 28.82% over five years). Trailing 4-quarter net profit (6434 USD m) is well above the FY25 figure (4335 USD m), so profit is moving fast and the cause is untested.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis needs growth to justify a 135.68x trailing P/E, yet revenue growth is already slowing (3-year CAGR 13.64% vs 28.82% over five years) and returns are low (ROE 7.19%, ROCE 6.49%). It would be wrong if revenue growth fell toward the 5% break line, or if margins slipped back to the pre-expansion level. The thresholds are lenient: the operating-margin kill line of 6% is below the roughly 7.2% starting point, so it would only trip after the whole three-year gain is gone. The D4 ROCE warn line of 5% sits below today's level. In the investor's own holdings, only Tesla and e.l.f. trade at higher P/Es. What would change this view: Evidence that revenue growth is re-accelerating and that trailing profit growth is backed by cash flow, with ROCE rising well above its current level, would justify the multiple and remove my objection.
